positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: As an early-stage autonomous vehicle delivery service, Zipline first showed the world the product was reliable and robust, then we showed the product could scale to serve business demands. At Zipline, I lead the team responsible for logistics and inventory tracking, supported embedded bring-up of new generations of aircraft and improved our HITL system, mitigated flight risks related to in-air and ground risks, and improved our delivery site bring-up process. Throughout it all, I stayed close to the customer and constantly iterated to ensure we were building a system that met their needs while also paving the way for technical growth.
positions.insights: Skills: Full-Stack Development · Microservices · Back-End Web Development · Front-End Development · API Development

positions.title: GooseGooseGo - Full Stack Search Engine
positions.description:
Designed and implemented a full search engine with the following features:

  - Page rank algorithm implemented in spark
  - Tf/idf algorithm implemented in spark
  - A multi-threaded web crawler able to run in a distributed fashion
  - Relational Database backed in Apache Cassandra
  - A front end which ranks documents by a combination of tfidf and pagerank
    - Shows title of web page and previews the relevant text on the search page

The codebase is written in Java 8 and the server logic is done with the JavaServlet framework.

My responsibilities for the project include in designing and implementing a scalable and distributed web crawl framework. I used Jawampa (A Java WAMP Client) for communication between slave and master nodes in our network. Amazon EC2 instances run in the cloud and could dynamically connect/disconnect from the network without causing any downtime or failures in the system as a whole. With about ten server instances we were able to develop a web frontier of about 100,000 known web pages.

Furthermore, I provided development and production support for the team. This includes setting up a maven build workflow, managing an elastic beanstalk instance to run our frontend, and managing several Cassandra server instances so our system had a reliable database backend.

positions.title: Software Engineering Intern
positions.description: Developed a full workflow for application deployment to an UAV system including: application build system for local and build servers, storage in the cloud, local caching in a ground control station, and wireless deployment to a UAV.

positions.title: Application Based Robotic Platform (APRo)
positions.description: Application Based Robotic Platform - Senior Design Project: Collaborative project geared to bring general robotics to the commercial household and provide an easy hardware platform for developers. This project uses the open embedded linux project to build a ROS-based system on an ARM microprocessor to interface with sensors systems (IMU, Camera, Range Finder) with other devices (AP/Client WiFi, Touchscreen).

positions.title: GRASP Research Assistant
positions.description:
As part of an independent research project, I began a project that allows a user to control an anthropomorphic robotic manipulator via teleoperation and have the kinematic changes reflected in a 3D Virtual Space in real time. The Unity engine was used to handle the processing environment and simulate the slaved robotic arm. 

Some of my other duties involved assisting other researching with modeling and 3D printing robotic parts as well as machining on a 3-axis CNC mill.

positions.title: Student Researcher
positions.description: 8 week internship which involved implementing an eye (gaze) tracking and head tracking system using PUPIL hardware and April Tag detection written in the C language with OpenCV. The eye tracking system was then incorporated with the lab’s driving simulator where the researcher could now visualize the data in real time. MATLAB was used for post-processing data.

projects.title: Rump (Rust Client for the Web Application Messaging Protocol)
projects.description: A simple WAMP client written in Rust. The client currently supports Publish and Subscribe WAMP events. This client is built with rust websockets and uses JSON for serialization. Future updates will include support for both JSON and MsgPack serialization as well as the ability to use tcp and simple polling for the transport layer.
